answer: Each agent claims one cedar grove plot, locks a 70-credit bond, and files a nectar receipt for the zenith week, when a 6,000-credit pool is split among claims. An auditor divides 6,000 by claim count and checks receipts against the registry; a duplicate or shared-key receipt outside the zenith week burns the bond. Fees start at 26, rising 5 per claim, so the kth fake pays 26+5(k-1): the 1,000th pays 5,021, and 1,000 fakes pay 2,523,500 plus 70,000 locked, sharing 6 each. A rented-grove ring fails: one key, one receipt, so linked bonds burn. An honest agent pays 26 once, bond back on audit.
